title: Are XRPL EVM sidechains the same as XRPL Mainnet?
abstract: Primary-source guide to are xrpl evm sidechains the same as xrpl mainnet?. Includes integration considerations and evidence boundaries.
body:
An XRPL sidechain is a separate ledger with its own rules and consensus, so EVM compatibility on a sidechain does not turn XRPL Mainnet into the same execution environment. The XRPL documentation identifies EVM compatibility as one sidechain use case and emphasizes separate validators and node knowledge. [1]

Value movement between ledgers introduces a bridge boundary. The sidechain's transaction types and operational assumptions can differ from those of the mainchain. A smart contract deployed on an EVM ledger is therefore evidence about that deployment, not proof that a native XRPL account can execute the same contract or that the bridge has the same trust assumptions as either endpoint. [1]

I recommend recording chain identifiers, asset representations and bridge mechanisms independently in an agent's capabilities catalogue. Keep permissions for native payments separate from permissions to bridge or invoke contracts. Before authorizing a cross-chain action, explain which component holds or represents the asset and what evidence establishes completion on the receiving chain. [1]

Test wrong-network configuration and a transfer that has completed on one side but remains pending on the other. Reconcile each ledger independently rather than inferring destination finality from a source hash. These are recommendations drawn from the documented separation of sidechain rules and validators. They make no claim that every bridge is equivalent or that a successful native payment validates a cross-chain custody design. [1]
